---
title: "Research data in full texts"
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: cosmo
    nav-buttons: []
    include-after-body:
      text: |
        <script>
        // Plotly measures text (legends, value labels) while a dashboard card is still hidden and
        // caches the zero widths per font. Once a chart is visible, a tiny font-name change forces a
        // fresh measurement -- on load and whenever a dashboard page or card tab is shown.
        function dvRedraw() {
          document.querySelectorAll('.js-plotly-plot').forEach(function (el) {
            if (el.clientWidth > 0 && el.offsetParent !== null && !el.dataset.dvDone) {
              el.dataset.dvDone = '1';
              Plotly.relayout(el, {'font.family': el._fullLayout.font.family + ', Arial'});
            }
          });
        }
        window.addEventListener('load', function () { setTimeout(dvRedraw, 200); });
        document.addEventListener('shown.bs.tab', function () { setTimeout(dvRedraw, 50); });

        // "How to read" hovers: each chart cell writes a hidden <div class="dv-help"> (Python how()).
        // Move it into a footer line of its card (or of the card named in data-for, e.g. a value box)
        // and show the text as a popover on hover / keyboard focus.
        function dvHelp() {
          document.querySelectorAll('.dv-help').forEach(function (h) {
            var html = h.innerHTML, target = h.dataset.for, card = null;
            if (target) {
              card = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bslib-value-box, .card')).find(function (c) {
                var t = c.querySelector('.value-box-title, .card-header, .card-title');
                return t && t.textContent.indexOf(target) >= 0;
              });
            } else { card = h.closest('.card'); }
            var out = h.closest('.cell-output-display') || h.parentElement;
            h.remove();
            if (out && !out.textContent.trim() && !out.querySelector('.js-plotly-plot, table, img, svg')) out.remove();
            if (!card) return;
            var foot = document.createElement('div'); foot.className = 'dv-help-foot';
            var a = document.createElement('span'); a.className = 'dv-help-link'; a.tabIndex = 0;
            a.setAttribute('role', 'button'); a.innerHTML = '&#9432; How to read';
            foot.appendChild(a); card.appendChild(foot);
            if (window.bootstrap && bootstrap.Popover) {
              new bootstrap.Popover(a, {content: html, html: true, trigger: 'hover focus', placement: 'top',
                                        container: 'body', customClass: 'dv-pop'});
            } else { a.title = h.textContent; }
          });
          window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'));
        }
        // after Quarto/bslib have built the cards (they rearrange the DOM on load)
        window.addEventListener('load', function () { setTimeout(dvHelp, 100); });
        </script>
        <style>
        .dv-help-foot { flex: none !important; padding: 2px 12px 6px; font-size: .8rem; }
        .dv-help-link { color: #2a78d6; cursor: help; border-bottom: 1px dotted #2a78d6; }
        .dv-pop { max-width: 440px; font-size: .85rem; }
        .dv-pop ul { padding-left: 1.1rem; margin: .3rem 0 0; }
        .bslib-value-box .dv-help-foot { position: absolute; bottom: 2px; right: 8px; padding: 0; z-index: 5; }
        /* six value boxes in a row make each < 300px wide, where bslib stacks the icon above the text and
           the row's fixed height crops it: keep icon left, text right, down to 180px */
        @container bslib-value-box (max-width: 300px) and (min-width: 180px) {
          .bslib-value-box:not(.showcase-bottom) .value-box-grid {
            grid-template-columns: 22% 1fr !important; grid-template-rows: 1fr !important;
            grid-template-areas: "left right" !important; }
          .bslib-value-box:not(.showcase-bottom) .value-box-grid .value-box-showcase { grid-area: left !important; padding: 0 0 0 .5rem !important; }
          .bslib-value-box:not(.showcase-bottom) .value-box-grid .value-box-area { grid-area: right !important; }
        }
        </style>
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
---

```{python}
#| include: false
# Reads the pipeline's own outputs -- nothing is recomputed or looked up here.
# Folder: DV_OUT_DIR (same variable as run_pipeline.py), else ../output.
# Every chart card has a "Data" tab: the rows behind the chart + CSV downloads (counts and rows).
import os, re, urllib.parse
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import Markdown, HTML

OUT = os.environ.get("DV_OUT_DIR") or os.path.join("..", "output")
S = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "summary.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype=str).fillna("")
D = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "per_dataset.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype=str).fillna("")

# ---- verdict categories: fixed order + fixed colours (colour follows the category, never its rank)
# Shared own data is split by access: deposited with restricted access still counts as shared
# ("as open as possible, as closed as necessary"), but is never shown as open. Same blue hue, lighter.
SHARED, SH_RESTR, SH_UNK = ("shared own data (open)", "shared own data (restricted access)",
                            "shared own data (access unknown)")
REGONLY, REUSE, DECL, NONE = ("no data in paper; dataset linked via DataCite", "reuses data only",
                              "declared, unverifiable", "no data found")
NOGEN  = "no data generated (paper says so)"   # nodata.py: the paper's own words
ONREQ  = "own data on request only (not shared)"  # nodata.on_request: data exist, not deposited
INSUPP = "own data in article / supplement only (not deposited)"  # nodata.supplement: data in the SI
# REGONLY is no longer a verdict (DataCite-only links are on Tool check); its colour is still used there
ORDER  = [SHARED, SH_RESTR, SH_UNK, INSUPP, ONREQ, REUSE, DECL, NOGEN, NONE]
LABEL  = {SHARED: "Shares own data: open", SH_RESTR: "Shares own data: restricted access",
          SH_UNK: "Shares own data: access unknown", INSUPP: "Own data in article / supplement only (not deposited)",
          ONREQ: "Own data on request only (not shared)", REGONLY: "DataCite link only (not counted)",
          REUSE: "Reuses data only", DECL: "Declared, not verifiable",
          NOGEN: "No data generated (paper says so)", NONE: "No data found (not shared, or no data)"}
# the two "no data" categories share the gray family; lighter = the paper explains it has none
COLOR  = {SHARED: "#2a78d6", SH_RESTR: "#86b6ef", SH_UNK: "#cde2fb", ONREQ: "#6250d6", INSUPP: "#c4559f", REGONLY: "#eb6834", REUSE: "#1baf7a",
          DECL: "#eda100", NOGEN: "#dedcd3", NONE: "#b4b2a8"}
# Colour rule: verdict colours (COLOR) mean the same everywhere -- blue family = shares own data (dark
# open, light restricted), purple/magenta = own data not deposited, green = reuse, yellow = declared,
# warm grays = no data. Things that are not verdicts (statements, tool-check groups) use cool slate.
SLATE = ["#3d4f63", "#7b8ca0", "#c4cdd8"]
INK, INK2, GRID, SURF ="#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e8e7e3", "#fcfcfb"

def style(fig, h=None):
    fig.update_layout(template="plotly_white", font=dict(family="'Source Sans Pro', 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif", size=13, color=INK2),
                      paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", barcornerradius=4,
                      margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=8, b=8), height=h, hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor="white", font_color=INK),
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.15, x=0, title=None, traceorder="normal"))
    fig.update_xaxes(gridcolor=GRID, zeroline=False, linecolor=GRID)
    fig.update_yaxes(gridcolor=GRID, zeroline=False, linecolor=GRID)
    return fig

def pct(a, b): return f"{100 * a / b:.0f}%" if b else "–"

def how(html, card=None):
    """The "How to read" hover of a chart: a hidden div that a script in the page header moves into a
    footer line of this cell's card (or of the card whose title contains `card`, e.g. a value box).
    Keep it short and in plain words: the readers are not all native English speakers."""
    attr = f' data-for="{card}"' if card else ""
    return HTML(f'<div class="dv-help" hidden{attr}>{html}</div>')

def _csv_link(df, label, filename):
    """A download button with the CSV inlined as a data: URI (BOM so Excel reads UTF-8)."""
    uri = "data:text/csv;charset=utf-8," + urllib.parse.quote("﻿" + df.to_csv(index=False))
    return (f'<a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" style="display:inline-block !important;width:auto !important;flex:0 0 auto !important" '
            f'download="{filename}" href="{uri}">{label}</a>')

def data_tab(rows, name, counts=None):
    """Data tab of a chart card: download buttons + the rows behind the chart, as a table.
    The table scrolls in its own box, so the dashboard's sticky table header can't cover the buttons."""
    btns = _csv_link(rows, f"Download rows ({len(rows)}) as CSV", f"{name}_rows.csv")
    if counts is not None:
        btns = _csv_link(counts, "Download counts (as in the chart) as CSV", f"{name}_counts.csv") + btns
    table = rows.to_html(index=False, border=0, escape=True, classes="table table-sm table-striped small")
    return HTML('<div style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;height:100%;min-height:0">'
                f'<div style="display:flex !important;flex-direction:row !important;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;'
                f'padding-bottom:8px;flex:none !important">{btns}</div>'
                f'<div style="flex:1;min-height:0;overflow:auto">{table}</div></div>')

# ---- paper level
# Papers that say they generated no data have nothing to share: they are left out of the charts and of
# the shares (user, 2026-11-10), so "no data found" only holds papers that might have had data.
# ORDER without NOGEN -> their `verdict` is NaN and every groupby on it skips them.
S["verdict"] = pd.Categorical(S["data_verdict"], [v for v in ORDER if v != NOGEN], ordered=True)
S["key"] = S["paper"].str.replace(r"\.[^.]+$", "", regex=True).str.lower()
NAME = dict(zip(S.key, S.paper))                    # per_dataset's paper key -> file name
N = len(S)
n_nogen  = int((S.data_verdict == NOGEN).sum())
NB = N - n_nogen                                    # base for shares: papers that may have data
n_shared = int(S.data_verdict.str.startswith("shared own data").sum())   # open + restricted access
n_open   = int((S.data_verdict == SHARED).sum())
n_req    = int((S.on_request_signal != "").sum())                         # "available on request"
n_supp   = int((S.supplement_signal != "").sum()) if "supplement_signal" in S else 0   # data in article / SI
CHART = [v for v in ORDER if v != NOGEN]            # verdicts shown in the charts

AREAS = {"1": "Natural sciences", "2": "Engineering & technology", "3": "Medical & health sciences",
         "4": "Agricultural & veterinary sciences", "5": "Social sciences", "6": "Humanities & the arts"}
def areas(row):
    """SSIF area = first digit of each Swepub code. A paper with codes in two areas counts in both."""
    if row.field_source.startswith("swepub"):
        return sorted({AREAS.get(c[0], "Other") for c in re.findall(r"(?:^|; )(\d{1,5})\b", row.field)})
    # 'swepub (SSIF)' and 'swepub classify (SSIF, automatic)' both carry SSIF codes (matched above).
    # OpenAlex topics (ASJC) don't map 1:1 onto SSIF, so they are not forced into an SSIF area here.
    return ["No SSIF field"]
S["areas"] = S.apply(areas, axis=1)

# ---- dataset level: datasets the papers share as their own (counted)
D["counted"] = (D.status == "confirmed") & (D.provenance == "own")
OWN = D[D.counted].merge(S[["key", "year"]], left_on="paper", right_on="key", how="left")
OWN["paper"] = OWN.paper.map(lambda k: NAME.get(k, k))
```

```{python}
#| title: "Papers per publication year, by data verdict"
yr = S[S.year != ""].groupby(["year", "verdict"], observed=False).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
fig = go.Figure()
for v in ORDER:
    if v in yr and yr[v].sum():
        _ = fig.add_bar(x=yr.index, y=yr[v], name=LABEL[v], marker=dict(color=COLOR[v], line=dict(color=SURF, width=2)),
                    hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y} paper(s)<extra>" + LABEL[v] + "</extra>")
_ = fig.update_layout(barmode="stack", xaxis=dict(type="category"),
                  updatemenus=[dict(type="buttons", direction="right", x=0, xanchor="left", y=1.12, showactive=True,
                                    bgcolor="white", bordercolor=GRID, font=dict(size=12),
                                    buttons=[dict(label="Count", method="relayout", args=[{"barnorm": ""}]),
                                             dict(label="Percent", method="relayout", args=[{"barnorm": "percent"}])])])
_ = style(fig).update_layout(margin=dict(t=36))
display(fig)
# value-box hover (value boxes can't hold extra output; placed by title)
display(how("The paper says its data are in the article itself or in its supplementary files, for example "
            "“All data are included in this article and its supplementary information”.<br>"
            "<b>Not counted as shared</b>: supplements have no DOI of their own and are often PDF files. "
            "Journals advise a data repository instead.<br>A paper that only says “supplementary material is "
            "available online” is not counted here: that could be figures, not data.",
            card="Say data are in the article"))
how("Each bar is the papers published that year, coloured by result. <b>Percent</b> shows shares "
    "instead of numbers.<br><b>Shares own data</b>: the paper says where the authors' own data is, and "
    "the link works. Open and restricted access (e.g. personal data) both count.<br>"
    "The <b>Data</b> tab has the rows behind the chart, also as CSV.")
```

```{python}
#| title: "Data verdict, all papers"
vc = S.verdict.value_counts().reindex(CHART).fillna(0).astype(int)
# one bar per result; the three "shares own data" kinds are one bar, stacked (open and restricted access
# are both sharing), so the bar length is all sharing papers
SHARE_ROW = "Shares own data"
row_of = {v: (SHARE_ROW if v in (SHARED, SH_RESTR, SH_UNK) else LABEL[v]) for v in CHART}
rows_y = list(dict.fromkeys(row_of[v] for v in CHART if vc[v] > 0))[::-1]       # top = first
fig = go.Figure()
for v in CHART:
    if vc[v] > 0:
        _ = fig.add_bar(y=[row_of[v]], x=[vc[v]], orientation="h", name=LABEL[v],
                        marker=dict(color=COLOR[v], line=dict(color=SURF, width=2)),
                        hovertemplate=f"{LABEL[v]}: %{{x}} paper(s) ({pct(vc[v], NB)})<extra></extra>")
tot = {r: sum(int(vc[v]) for v in CHART if row_of[v] == r) for r in rows_y}
for r in rows_y:
    _ = fig.add_annotation(x=tot[r], y=r, text=f"{tot[r]}  ({pct(tot[r], NB)})", showarrow=False,
                           xanchor="left", xshift=6, font=dict(color=INK2))
_ = style(fig).update_layout(barmode="stack", showlegend=False,
                             xaxis=dict(visible=False, range=[0, max(tot.values()) * 1.35]),
                             yaxis=dict(categoryorder="array", categoryarray=rows_y))
display(fig)
how("One result per paper:<ul>"
    "<li><b>Shares own data</b>: the paper points to the authors' own data and the link works. One bar: "
    "dark blue = open, light blue = restricted access (e.g. personal data). Both count as shared.</li>"
    "<li><b>In article / supplement only</b>: the paper says its data are in the article or its "
    "supplementary files, not in a repository. Not counted as shared.</li>"
    "<li><b>On request only</b>: the paper says the data can be asked for, but they are not stored "
    "anywhere. Not counted as shared.</li>"
    "<li><b>Reuses data only</b>: only other people's data.</li>"
    "<li><b>Declared, not verifiable</b>: the paper mentions data, but the link does not work.</li>"
    "<li><b>No data found</b>: the rest. Not shared, or no data: the tool can't tell which.</li></ul>"
    f"Papers that say they generated no data ({n_nogen} this run) have nothing to share, so they are left "
    f"out of all charts and percentages: shares are of {NB} papers, not {N}. They are listed in the Papers "
    "table.<br>"
    "The result is about what the paper says. Datasets that only DataCite links to a paper are on the "
    "<b>Tool check</b> page.")
```

```{python}
#| title: "Restricted access: own datasets vs their own repositories, by research field"
# From field_norm.py (optional): each own DataCite dataset next to the other datasets in ITS repository,
# in the SSIF area of the citing paper (or the whole repository when the repository sets no subjects or
# the area is small). Expected = mean of those references over the datasets. Same rules on both sides.
FN_PATH = os.path.join(OUT, "field_norm_datasets.csv")
HAVE_NORM = os.path.exists(FN_PATH)
if HAVE_NORM:
    FD = pd.read_csv(FN_PATH, encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype={"ssif_area": str})
    FD["paper"] = FD.paper.map(lambda k: NAME.get(k, k))
    FC = FD[FD.reference.notna()].copy()                                   # DataCite datasets only
    FC["area_label"] = FC.ssif_area.map(AREAS).fillna("No SSIF field")
    ALL_OWN = "All own datasets"
    groups = [ALL_OWN] + [a for a in AREAS.values() if a in set(FC.area_label)]
    def refs_text(g):
        c = g.groupby(["repository", "reference"]).size()
        return "<br>".join(f"{r} ({how}): {n}" for (r, how), n in c.items())
    o, e = dict(y=[], text=[], customdata=[]), dict(y=[], text=[], customdata=[])
    for gname in groups:
        if gname == ALL_OWN:          # one row per dataset: average its references over its areas
            g = FC.groupby("identifier").agg(restricted=("restricted", "first"),
                                             ref_share_restricted=("ref_share_restricted", "mean"),
                                             repository=("repository", "first"),
                                             reference=("reference", "first")).reset_index()
        else:
            g = FC[FC.area_label == gname]
        k, n = int(g.restricted.sum()), len(g)
        o["y"].append(100 * k / n); o["text"].append(f"{k}/{n}")
        o["customdata"].append(f"{k} of {n} own dataset(s)")
        ev = 100 * g.ref_share_restricted.mean()
        e["y"].append(ev); e["text"].append(f"{ev:.0f}%")
        e["customdata"].append("references used (datasets):<br>" + refs_text(g))
    NAMES = ["Own datasets in these papers", "Expected from their repositories"]
    fig = go.Figure([go.Bar(x=groups, y=t["y"], text=t["text"], customdata=t["customdata"], name=nm,
                            marker_color=c, textposition="outside", textfont=dict(color=INK2, size=11),
                            cliponaxis=False,
                            hovertemplate="<b>%{x}</b><br>" + nm + ": %{y:.0f}%<br>%{customdata}<extra></extra>")
                     for t, nm, c in zip([o, e], NAMES, [COLOR[SHARED], "#8d8b84"])])
    _ = fig.update_layout(barmode="group", bargap=0.3, bargroupgap=0.08)
    _ = style(fig).update_layout(yaxis=dict(ticksuffix="%", range=[0, 100],
                                            title=dict(text="% of datasets with restricted access")))
    display(fig)
    display(how("Share of datasets with <b>restricted access</b> (e.g. personal data; access on "
                "application). The rest are open.<br><b>Blue</b>: the datasets in these papers. "
                "<b>Grey</b>: what is usual in the same repositories, in the same field (all their "
                "datasets in DataCite; the whole repository if it has no field information). Hover a bar "
                "to see which.<br>Only fields with at least one own dataset in DataCite are shown, so "
                "there can be fewer fields than in the research field chart.<br>"
                "About datasets, not papers. Few datasets per field (k/n): read as "
                "examples, not trends. Update with <i>python field_norm.py</i>."))
else:
    display(Markdown("No reference yet. Run `python field_norm.py` after the pipeline (asks DataCite, a "
                     "few minutes) to write `field_norm.csv` and `field_norm_datasets.csv`, then render again."))
```

```{python}
#| title: "Data availability statement, by data verdict"
# has_das = found by pattern search (heading) or by the LLM; both are in summary.csv
DASL = {"yes": "Has a data availability statement", "no": "No data availability statement"}
dv = S.groupby(["has_das", "verdict"], observed=False).size().unstack(fill_value=0).reindex(["no", "yes"]).fillna(0)
fig = go.Figure()
for v in ORDER:
    if v in dv and dv[v].sum():
        _ = fig.add_bar(y=[f"{DASL[k]} ({int(dv.loc[k].sum())})" for k in dv.index], x=dv[v], orientation="h",
                        name=LABEL[v], marker=dict(color=COLOR[v], line=dict(color=SURF, width=2)),
                        hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x} paper(s)<extra>" + LABEL[v] + "</extra>")
_ = fig.update_layout(barmode="stack",
                      updatemenus=[dict(type="buttons", direction="right", x=0, xanchor="left", y=1.12, showactive=True,
                                        bgcolor="white", bordercolor=GRID, font=dict(size=12),
                                        buttons=[dict(label="Count", method="relayout", args=[{"barnorm": ""}]),
                                                 dict(label="Percent", method="relayout", args=[{"barnorm": "percent"}])])])
_ = style(fig).update_layout(margin=dict(t=36), legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.12, traceorder="normal"))
display(fig)
how("Does the paper have a <b>data availability statement</b> (a section that says where the data are, "
    "e.g. “Data availability”, “Data accessibility”, “Availability of data and materials”)? Found by "
    "pattern search on the heading, or by the LLM. Colours as on the Overview page: do papers with a "
    "statement share their data more often?<br>A statement is not the same as shared data: it can also say "
    "“on request” or “not applicable”.")
```

```{python}
# repository = the DataCite client that registered the DOI; publisher (in the hover) = the institution.
# Access from DataCite's access rights (no access right stated = open, as in the pipeline).
ACCL = {"open": "Open", "restricted": "Restricted access", "": "Access unknown"}
ACCC = {"open": COLOR[SHARED], "restricted": COLOR[SH_RESTR], "": COLOR[SH_UNK]}
RO = OWN.assign(repository=OWN.repository.replace("", "(unknown)"),
                acc=OWN.openness.where(OWN.openness.isin(["open", "restricted"]), ""))
rt = RO.groupby(["repository", "acc"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0).reindex(columns=list(ACCL), fill_value=0)
rt = rt.assign(n=rt.sum(axis=1)).sort_values("n")
pubs = RO.groupby("repository").publisher.agg(lambda s: "<br>".join(sorted({p for p in s if p})) or "–")
fig = go.Figure()
for k, lab in ACCL.items():
    if rt[k].sum():
        _ = fig.add_bar(y=rt.index, x=rt[k], orientation="h", name=lab, customdata=pubs.reindex(rt.index),
                        marker=dict(color=ACCC[k], line=dict(color=SURF, width=2)),
                        hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b>: %{x} dataset(s)<br>publisher:<br>%{customdata}<extra>" + lab + "</extra>")
_ = style(fig).update_layout(barmode="stack", legend=dict(y=-0.15))
display(fig)
how("Where the authors' own datasets are stored: the repository that registered the dataset's DOI "
    "(e.g. SND, Chalmers DORIS, Zenodo), split by access. <b>Restricted access</b>: deposited, but access "
    "on conditions (e.g. personal data); still counted as shared.<br>Hover a bar to see the responsible "
    "institution. Archives without DOIs (e.g. ENA) show the archive.")
```

# Tool check {scrolling="true"}

```{python}
#| include: false
# Everything the tool itself is unsure about, as one to-do list: (paper, id, issue, what to do).
# Sources: per_dataset.csv, merged_output.csv (dv_disagreement), selfcheck.csv (answer key).
M = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "merged_output.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype=str).fillna("")
C = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "selfcheck.csv"), encoding="utf-8-sig", dtype=str).fillna("")
G_ID, G_TOOLS, G_PAPER = "Broken or missing ids", "LLM vs pattern search / registries", "Paper metadata"
rows = []
def add(group, issue, paper, ident, todo): rows.append(dict(group=group, issue=issue, paper=paper, identifier=ident, todo=todo))

cause = dict(zip(C.identifier, C.broken_id_cause))
for _, r in D[D.registry.str.startswith("repaired")].iterrows():
    written = r.registry[len("repaired (text had "):-1]
    cs = cause.get(r.identifier, "")
    if cs == "as-printed":
        add(G_ID, "Wrong id printed in the paper", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
            f"Paper prints {written}. Registered DOI used; worth reporting to authors / publisher")
    elif cs == "pdf-extraction":
        add(G_ID, "Id broken by PDF text extraction", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
            f"Text had {written}; the PDF itself is right. Registered DOI used, nothing to fix in the paper")
    else:
        add(G_ID, "Id repaired, cause not checked", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
            f"Text had {written}. Set DV_PDF_DIR to check the PDF")
for _, r in D[D.status == "likely-broken-link"].iterrows():
    add(G_ID, "Declared link does not resolve", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
        "Check by hand: typo, private/review link, or removed record")
for _, r in D[D.status == "likely-unchecked"].iterrows():
    add(G_ID, "Link could not be checked automatically", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
        "The site blocks automated checks. Open it by hand: does it work, and is it a published "
        "record (not a private or reviewer link)?")
for _, r in D[D.status == "likely-no-doi"].iterrows():
    add(G_ID, "Declared without a resolvable id", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper), r.identifier,
        "Data statement points to a site, not a record; check by hand")
for _, r in D[D.status == "homepage"].iterrows():
    add(G_ID, "Link to a repository's front page (paper also gives its own record)", NAME.get(r.paper, r.paper),
        r.identifier, "Probably the repository named next to its record, so not counted as a second dataset. "
        "Check only if the paper has data in two repositories")
for _, r in C[C.result.str.startswith("not found")].iterrows():
    add(G_TOOLS, "Known dataset not found in the text", r.paper, r.identifier,
        f"DataCite links it and the paper cites it as {r.cited_as}; neither the LLM nor pattern search found it")

for _, r in M[M.dv_disagreement != ""].iterrows():
    for part in r.dv_disagreement.split("; "):
        if part.startswith("detect:"):
            add(G_TOOLS, "Not found by the LLM, found by pattern search or DataCite", r.file, r.identifier,
                "Found by " + " + ".join({"llm": "LLM", "regex": "pattern search", "datacite": "DataCite",
                                          "text": "web link in text"}.get(t, t)
                                         for t in part.split("(found by ")[-1].rstrip(")").split("+")))
        elif part.startswith("isdata:"):
            add(G_TOOLS, "LLM says dataset, DOI registry says not a dataset", r.file, r.identifier,
                "Registry type: " + (r.dv_verdict.split("(")[-1].rstrip(")") or "?") + ". Usually a cited article; check if wanted")
        elif part.startswith("prov:"):
            add(G_TOOLS, "Own vs reused differs", r.file, r.identifier,
            part[len("prov: "):].replace("DFP=", "LLM: ").replace("DV=", "ORCID / author names: "))
        elif part.startswith("open:"):
            add(G_TOOLS, "Open vs restricted differs", r.file, r.identifier,
            part[len("open: "):].replace("DFP=", "LLM: ").replace("DV=", "DataCite access rights: "))

pdoi = M.groupby("file").agg(check=("dv_paper_doi_check", "first"), given=("paper_doi", "first"), doi=("dv_paper_doi", "first"))
for f, r in pdoi.iterrows():
    if r.check == "corrected":
        add(G_PAPER, "Paper DOI corrected by title check", f, r.doi, f"Given: {r.given or 'none'}. Check which is right")
    elif r.check == "found":
        add(G_PAPER, "Paper DOI found by title check", f, r.doi, "No DOI was given")
    elif r.check == "unconfirmed":
        add(G_PAPER, "Paper DOI not confirmed", f, r.given, "No DataCite lookup or field for this paper; check the DOI")
for p, g in D[D.status == "datacite-only"].groupby("paper"):
    add(G_PAPER, "DataCite links datasets the paper doesn't cite", NAME.get(p, p), f"{len(g)} dataset(s)",
        "Not counted. Check the published version, or the dataset's metadata")
# the paper says it has no data of its own, but the tool found own or declared data in it
for _, r in S[(S.no_data_signal != "") & (S.data_verdict.str.startswith("shared own data")
                                          | (S.data_verdict == DECL))].iterrows():
    add(G_PAPER, "Paper says it has no data, yet cites own data", r.paper, r.no_data_signal[:90],
        "Read the data statement: is the cited dataset the authors' own?")

# data availability statement: the LLM and the pattern search (heading) disagree
for _, r in S[(S.das_llm != "") & ((S.das_pattern != "") != (S.das_llm == "yes"))].iterrows():
    if r.das_pattern:
        add(G_TOOLS, "Data availability statement: found by pattern search, not by the LLM", r.paper,
            r.das_pattern, "Check the heading in the paper: is it a data availability statement?")
    else:
        add(G_TOOLS, "Data availability statement: found by the LLM, not by pattern search", r.paper, "",
            "Check the paper: which heading does it use? (A new wording could be added to the search.)")

Q = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["group", "issue", "paper", "identifier", "todo"])
# issue groups are not verdicts, so they get neutral slate shades, not verdict colours
GCOL = {G_ID: SLATE[0], G_TOOLS: SLATE[1], G_PAPER: SLATE[2]}
```

```{python}
#| title: "Who found each dataset (in the text, or only via DataCite)"
def finder(src):
    s = set(src.split("+"))
    if "llm" in s and "regex" in s: return "Both text searches (LLM + pattern search)"
    if "llm" in s:                  return "LLM only"
    if "regex" in s:                return "Pattern search only"
    if "text" in s:                 return "Found via DataCite; paper gives a web link, not the DOI"
    return "Only in DataCite; paper doesn't mention it (not counted)"
FIND = ["Both text searches (LLM + pattern search)", "LLM only", "Pattern search only",
        "Found via DataCite; paper gives a web link, not the DOI", "Only in DataCite; paper doesn't mention it (not counted)"]
R = D[D.status.isin(["confirmed", "datacite-only"]) | D.status.str.startswith("likely")].copy()
R["finder"] = R.source.map(finder)
R["kind2"] = R.status.map(lambda s: "Verified dataset" if s == "confirmed" else
                          ("DataCite link only (not counted)" if s == "datacite-only" else "Declared, not verifiable"))
ft = R.groupby(["finder", "kind2"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0).reindex(FIND[::-1]).fillna(0).astype(int)
fig = go.Figure()
for k, col in [("Verified dataset", COLOR[SHARED]), ("DataCite link only (not counted)", COLOR[REGONLY]),
               ("Declared, not verifiable", COLOR[DECL])]:
    if k in ft and ft[k].sum():
        _ = fig.add_bar(y=ft.index, x=ft[k], orientation="h", name=f"{k} ({int(ft[k].sum())})",
                        marker=dict(color=col, line=dict(color=SURF, width=2)),
                        hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x}<extra>" + k + "</extra>")
_ = style(fig).update_layout(barmode="stack", legend=dict(y=-0.2))
display(fig)
display(how("How each dataset was found:<ul>"
            "<li><b>LLM</b>: a large language model reads the paper and lists the data it mentions.</li>"
            "<li><b>Pattern search</b>: a rule-based search (regular expressions) of the same text, for DOIs and archive "
            "numbers (e.g. PRJEB84056).</li>"
            "<li><b>DataCite</b>: the other way round. The dataset's record says it belongs to the paper. It "
            "counts only if the paper also mentions the dataset (e.g. by web link).</li></ul>"
            "The <b>Data</b> tab has the rows behind the chart, also as CSV."))
# value boxes can't hold extra text, so their hovers are written here and placed by title (data-for)
n_dfp = int(C.found_by.str.contains("DFP").sum())
n_pat = int(C.found_by.str.contains("regex").sum())
WHY = {"landing page": "the paper gives the dataset's web page, not its DOI",
       "doi (malformed)": "the dataset link in the text is broken"}
missed = [f"{NAME.get(str(r.paper).rsplit('.', 1)[0].lower(), r.paper)} ({WHY.get(r.cited_as, r.cited_as)})"
          for r in C[~C.result.str.startswith("found")].itertuples()]
display(how("Normally we can't know which datasets a paper <i>should</i> have. One exception: the dataset's "
            "record in DataCite says it belongs to the paper, <b>and</b> the paper cites it. Then the right "
            "answer is certain, so these datasets are a small test for the two text searches.<br>"
            f"<b>This run:</b> {len(C)} such datasets. Found {n_found}: LLM {n_dfp}, pattern search {n_pat}. "
            + ("Missed: " + "; ".join(missed) + "." if missed else "None missed.") + "<br>"
            "<b>Limits:</b> only repositories that record the link back to the paper take part (mostly SND "
            "and Chalmers DORIS). It shows how often the searches <i>miss</i> data, not how often they report "
            "something that isn't data.", card="Self-check"))
display(how("<b>repaired</b>: a broken dataset link that the tool fixed automatically (it matches a "
            "registered DOI).<br><b>dead</b>: a dataset link in the paper that does not work (page or record "
            "not found).<br>"
            "<b>no id</b>: the paper mentions data, but gives no link.", card="Broken ids"))
display(how("Rows where the LLM and the other checks give different answers: is it a dataset (DOI "
            "registry), is it the authors' own (ORCID and author names), is it open or restricted (DataCite "
            "access rights), or found only by pattern search. Listed row by row in the table below.",
            card="Rows where the LLM"))
```
